metas.name: Army of Shadows
metas.description: Captures resistance as cold, lonely procedure. French Resistance, 1942: safe houses, coded phrases, informers executed badly — no glamour and almost no hope, filmed like a heist movie in mourning.

metas.name: Paths of Glory
metas.description: Captures military honour used to cover a command failure. After a suicidal attack fails, three soldiers are chosen to be executed for cowardice to make the point, and their colonel tries law against arithmetic.

metas.name: Microcosmos
metas.description: Captures a meadow as an alien world, at insect scale. One day in a French field, almost no narration: snails mating, a dung beetle rolling its ball uphill, rain arriving like artillery.

metas.name: Koyaanisqatsi
metas.description: Captures civilisation as pattern. No dialogue or characters: time-lapse clouds, highways, factories, demolition and crowds cut to Philip Glass, until modern life starts to look like weather.

metas.name: Leviathan
metas.description: Captures commercial fishing as a sensory ordeal. Cameras strapped to nets, chains, helmets and the hull of a North Atlantic trawler — fish heads, gulls, diesel, men half-asleep at 3 a.m., no explanation offered.

metas.name: Apollo 13
metas.description: Captures competence under constraint. An explosion in space, and the film becomes people in rooms with slide rules solving the next physical problem before the air runs out — the opposite of lone-hero cinema.

metas.name: First Man
metas.description: Captures the Moon landing from inside a grieving, taciturn man. Armstrong as an engineer who can land anything except in his own family's pain; the flights are rattling, cramped and procedural.

metas.name: Princess Mononoke
metas.description: Captures an ecological war with no pure side. Iron Town needs the forest cut to survive; the forest gods need the humans gone; a prince cursed by a dying god tries to see with unclouded eyes.

metas.name: Senna
metas.description: Captures speed, faith and charisma, entirely from archive. Ayrton Senna's career built only from period footage and voices — rivalry with Prost, Brazil on his helmet, in-car laps that feel like prayer at 300 km/h.

metas.name: Free Solo
metas.description: Captures a man whose relationship to fear is simply different from yours. Alex Honnold prepares to climb El Capitan without ropes while the filmmakers — his friends — argue on camera about whether filming changes the odds.

metas.name: When We Were Kings
metas.description: Captures Ali as a political and verbal artist at his peak. The Rumble in the Jungle, Zaire 1974: training footage, a music festival, Mobutu's stadium, and Ali talking everyone, including himself, into belief.

metas.name: The Wrestler
metas.description: Captures a body that only has value inside the ring. An ageing, hearing-damaged wrestler on supermarket shifts, trying with his daughter, and finding the crowd is the one place the world still makes sense to him.

metas.name: Raging Bull
metas.description: Captures self-destruction in a family kitchen as much as a ring. Jake LaMotta's jealousy and violence at home filmed with the same intensity as the fights; he can take any punch except accountability.

metas.name: Jiro Dreams of Sushi
metas.description: Captures mastery as repetition across a lifetime. An 85-year-old with a tiny Tokyo subway sushi counter and three Michelin stars, sons waiting to inherit, and a standard of 'delicious' he says he still hasn't reached.

metas.name: The 400 Blows
metas.description: Captures a boy being processed into a delinquent. Paris, a cramped flat, a teacher, small lies compounding into reform school — and a final run to the sea in one long take, ending on his face.

metas.name: Kes
metas.description: Captures a working-class kid with exactly one thing of his own. In Barnsley coal country, Billy is written off at home and school, teaches himself falconry from a library book, and a kestrel makes him articulate and gentle.

metas.name: Fish Tank
metas.description: Captures a teenage girl's anger and wanting in a place with no room for either. An Essex estate, a 15-year-old who dances alone in empty flats, and her mum's new boyfriend who seems to actually see her.

metas.name: Eighth Grade
metas.description: Captures social anxiety in the age of front-facing cameras, exactly. A girl filming confident advice videos she cannot follow, pool parties endured minute by minute, and a father scene near the end that rearranges parents.

metas.name: Pan's Labyrinth
metas.description: Captures a child's fantasy as the only available resistance. Spain, 1944: a girl with a fascist stepfather descends to a faun's tasks while the adult war continues above ground, and fantasy is never 'just' escape.

metas.name: The Night of the Hunter
metas.description: Captures childhood danger as a fairy tale. A preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles hunts two children down a river for hidden money; they flee by boat through a dreamlike, animal-watched night.

metas.name: All the President's Men
metas.description: Captures journalism as shoe leather. Watergate as phone calls, parking garages, notebooks and editors asking 'what else do you have?' — verification repeated until a presidency moves.

metas.name: Spotlight
metas.description: Captures an investigation as a team slowly realising the size of the room they're in. Boston Globe reporters, church abuse, sealed records, survivors telling it plainly — no heroics beyond persistence.

metas.name: The Insider
metas.description: Captures the cost of telling the truth inside two corporations at once. A tobacco scientist bound by confidentiality, a TV producer with a network to protect, and an interview everyone with money wants buried.

metas.name: Zodiac
metas.description: Captures obsession with a case that will not close. San Francisco, years of codes, files, basements and false certainties; the killer fades and the men who chased him are what's left damaged.

metas.name: Sicario
metas.description: Captures an idealist being used as a legal fig leaf. An FBI agent attached to a border operation she is not briefed on, a convoy into Juárez filmed like an occupying army, rules revealed only after she has broken them.

metas.name: Burning
metas.description: Captures class envy curdling into a mystery with no floor. In Seoul, a delivery kid, a girl who mimes eating a tangerine so well you see it, a rich man who burns abandoned greenhouses — and a disappearance the film will not solve.

metas.name: The Apartment
metas.description: Captures loneliness in a big company, and kindness as a decision. An insurance clerk lends his flat to executives for their affairs to get promoted, loves the elevator girl from afar, and hits Christmas at the lowest point of both.

metas.name: Amélie
metas.description: Captures a lonely young woman engineering small happinesses for strangers. Montmartre, a tin of childhood treasures returned to its owner, and a heroine who can fix everyone's life except ask for anything in her own.

metas.name: Singin' in the Rain
metas.description: Captures pure performed joy, inside a story about an industry panicking. Hollywood switching to sound, a star with a terrible voice, and musical numbers that still feel like showing off for the love of it.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description: Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

metas.name: Big Night
metas.description: Captures two brothers arguing about whether a meal should be art or business. Italian immigrants, a failing restaurant, one elaborate dinner to save it, and a final wordless scene of one cooking breakfast for the other.

metas.name: Rushmore
metas.description: Captures a precocious teenager's grandiosity as a grief strategy. A scholarship kid who runs every club and stages huge plays falls for a widowed teacher and goes to war with a sad industrialist who is, emotionally, the same age.

metas.name: Man with a Movie Camera
metas.description: Captures a city inventing cinema while cinema invents the city. A Soviet day from waking to work to leisure, no story, and editing tricks in every minute that films still use — nearly a century old and showing off.

metas.name: Sans Soleil
metas.description: Captures memory as footage you keep re-narrating. A woman reads a travelling cameraman's letters over images of Tokyo, Guinea-Bissau, Iceland and San Francisco, until a travel film becomes a film about how a mind stores the world.

metas.name: Los Angeles Plays Itself
metas.description: Captures a city through the lies movies told about it. A video essay built entirely from clips — how Los Angeles is used as backdrop, villain and stand-in for everywhere else — narrated by a resident who loves it and resents all of it.

metas.name: Close-Up
metas.description: Captures a poor film fan who wanted, briefly, to be the man whose name he borrowed. In Tehran a man impersonates a famous director to a family, is arrested, and then everyone involved re-enacts their own case, including the trial.

metas.name: Day for Night
metas.description: Captures a film set as a chaotic temporary family. Truffaut plays the director of a mediocre melodrama, keeping affairs, breakdowns, accidents and deadlines moving toward a finished film nobody thinks is great and everybody needs.

metas.name: News from Home
metas.description: Captures emigration as long shots and your mother's voice. New York — subways, diners, empty streets — while her mother's letters from Brussels, full of family news and worry, are read over it; homesickness with the geography reversed.

metas.name: Silence
metas.description: Captures faith tested by other people's suffering, not your own. Jesuit priests in 17th-century Japan, where Christians are tortured to make them apostatise and God does not answer — Scorsese's quietest, most unresolved film.

metas.name: Ordet
metas.description: Captures a household of different faiths waiting on a miracle nobody respectable believes in. A Danish farm: a strict father, a son who thinks he is Jesus, a beloved daughter-in-law — very slow and plain, then an ending argued about for 70 years.

metas.name: Winter Light
metas.description: Captures a pastor performing comfort he cannot feel. A small Swedish church, a fisherman terrified of nuclear war, a woman who has read the priest's coldness exactly — an hour and twenty minutes of winter afternoon.

metas.name: First Reformed
metas.description: Captures despair finding a political shape inside a small church. A minister keeping a diary in a historic church that is mostly a gift shop, and a young activist asking whether God can forgive us for what we've done to the world.

metas.name: Oslo, August 31st
metas.description: Captures a man visiting his own life while on leave from rehab. Job interview, old friends, a party, the family home for sale — Oslo in late summer light, conversations so ordinary they are painful for what he hears in them.

metas.name: Trainspotting
metas.description: Captures a heroin scene's energy before it shows you the bill. Edinburgh friends filmed like they're in the best movie ever, which is how it felt — until a baby, a toilet and a series of betrayals change the genre under them.

metas.name: Weekend
metas.description: Captures intimacy with an expiration date already on it. Two men meet in Nottingham on a Friday, one leaving the country on Sunday, and talk in bed, pubs and trains about sex, coming out, and how much of yourself you perform.

metas.name: God's Own Country
metas.description: Captures a man who can only express feeling through work and drink learning tenderness from lambing. A young Yorkshire farmer, mud and silence, and a Romanian migrant worker hired for the season who is gentle in a way he has no defences for.

metas.name: Brokeback Mountain
metas.description: Captures a love conducted in a few weeks a year, across twenty years. Wyoming herders, marriages and children in between, and a shirt kept in a closet doing more work than any speech.

metas.name: Taste of Cherry
metas.description: Captures ordinary conversation held against a decision to die. A man drives the hills outside Tehran offering money to whoever will bury him in the morning, picking up a soldier, a seminarian and a taxidermist who each answer differently; the ending breaks the film open on purpose.

metas.name: Under the Skin
metas.description: Captures human beings seen from outside the species. A woman drives a van around Glasgow picking up men, in real streets with hidden cameras and non-actors, and something in the routine begins to fail — images that lodge permanently.

metas.name: Her
metas.description: Captures loneliness in a warm, well-designed future. A divorced man who writes other people's love letters for a living falls for a voice in his ear, and the film takes the relationship seriously enough to let it outgrow him.

metas.name: Gattaca
metas.description: Captures a caste system built from a blood sample. A man born without genetic screening borrows another man's blood, urine and identity to reach space, while his 'valid' brother keeps challenging him to swimming races neither should survive.

metas.name: The Truman Show
metas.description: Captures a paranoia that turns out to be an accurate description. An insurance salesman in a seaside town so pleasant it feels laminated, a sky that malfunctions, and a dawning suspicion about everyone who loves him.

metas.name: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
metas.description: Captures trying to keep someone while paying to forget them. A couple erase each other after a breakup; inside the procedure, mid-deletion, he changes his mind and hides her in childhood memories the technicians haven't reached.

metas.name: Solaris
metas.description: Captures grief arriving in physical form, in orbit. A psychologist on a space station finds the crew haunted by visitors the planet below has made from their memories — including his dead wife, who knows she isn't her.

metas.name: Room
metas.description: Captures a child's entire world being eleven feet wide, and then it not being. A mother makes a complete, loving universe for her five-year-old inside the shed where they're held; the second half, outside, is the harder adjustment for both.

metas.name: Lady Bird
metas.description: Captures a mother and daughter who love each other in a way that keeps missing. Sacramento, a girl desperate to leave for the East Coast, a mother working double shifts, fights in moving cars, and a final voicemail that reframes every argument.

metas.name: All About My Mother
metas.description: Captures grief assembling a chosen family. After her son is killed, a Madrid nurse returns to Barcelona and gathers an actress, a nun and a trans sex worker from her past — melodrama played completely straight, and generous.

metas.name: Make Way for Tomorrow
metas.description: Captures old parents becoming an inconvenience to distribute. In the Depression a couple lose their house and their adult children split them between households 'temporarily' — politeness does the damage, and the farewell scene is unforgettable.

metas.name: Opening Night
metas.description: Captures an actress coming apart inside a role about ageing. Rehearsing a play in which her character must accept getting older — drinking, seeing the young fan who died outside the theatre — while the production needs her functional by Thursday.

metas.name: All About Eve
metas.description: Captures ambition wearing perfect manners. A young fan insinuates herself into a Broadway star's life one helpful errand at a time; the dialogue is the sharpest ever written for this, and every adult sees the game a moment too late.

metas.name: Tár
metas.description: Captures prestige as a system one woman believes she controls. A conductor at the top of classical music — Berlin, Mahler, acolytes — and a slow accumulation of recordings, edits and allegations, filmed with the cold precision its subject would admire.

metas.name: Funny Games
metas.description: Captures the audience's appetite, by refusing to feed it the usual way. Two polite young men hold a family at their holiday house; violence happens off-screen or gets rewound, and the film keeps asking why you're still watching.

metas.name: Atanarjuat: The Fast Runner
metas.description: Captures an Inuit oral epic told by the community it belongs to. Made in Igloolik, in Inuktitut, with a largely Inuit cast and crew: a rivalry, a murder, and a naked run across the ice told for centuries.

metas.name: Incendies
metas.description: Captures two children learning their mother's life was a war they knew nothing about. Montreal twins, a will, two sealed letters, and a journey into a fictionalised Lebanon their mother never described — it hits like a Greek tragedy.

metas.name: Mommy
metas.description: Captures a mother and son whose love is indistinguishable from the emergency. In Quebec, a widow, her volatile teenage son and a shy neighbour across the street — shot in a square frame that literally widens in the one scene where life briefly works.

metas.name: The Sweet Hereafter
metas.description: Captures a town after the worst thing has already happened. A school bus crash in small-town BC, a lawyer arriving to build a lawsuit, and grief looking for a shape that money keeps offering and failing to be.

metas.name: Videodrome
metas.description: Captures a TV signal getting inside a body. A sleazy Toronto cable programmer finds a pirate broadcast of torture, becomes obsessed, and his perception and flesh start reorganising around it.

metas.name: Stories We Tell
metas.description: Captures a family discovering its central story has an author problem. Sarah Polley interviews her own family about her late mother; the accounts agree on the love and diverge on everything else, then the film shows you its own construction.

metas.name: The Lives of Others
metas.description: Captures a surveillance officer changed by the lives he's assigned to transcribe. East Berlin, 1984: a Stasi captain bugs a playwright's flat, types his reports, and quietly begins to edit what the state gets to know.

metas.name: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
metas.description: Captures espionage as tired old men in bad rooms. A mole inside British intelligence, investigated through retirement-age sadness, Christmas parties and files — almost nothing explodes; the atmosphere is the action.

metas.name: The Third Man
metas.description: Captures friendship curdling in a ruined, divided city. Postwar Vienna: a pulp writer arrives to find his friend dead and getting saintlier the less sense the story makes — zither music, sewers, and the ferris wheel speech.

metas.name: Notorious
metas.description: Captures love being used as an intelligence asset. A woman is recruited to marry into a Nazi circle in Rio because of who her father was, by an agent unable to say the one thing that would make it bearable.

metas.name: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
metas.description: Captures Cold War spycraft as exhaustion and managed betrayal. A burnt agent is sent on one last operation that requires him to become genuinely washed up — the bleakest, most honest of the Le Carré films.

metas.name: Rififi
metas.description: Captures a robbery as manual labour. A Paris jewel heist whose centrepiece is roughly half an hour with no dialogue and no score — umbrellas, drills, plaster dust, men breathing — that every heist film since is quoting.

metas.name: The Killing
metas.description: Captures a perfect plan told in pieces that don't line up in time. A racetrack robbery replayed from each participant's angle, a suitcase of money, and an airport finale involving a small dog.

metas.name: Sexy Beast
metas.description: Captures menace arriving in a holiday villa. A retired gangster, happily fat and sunburned in Spain, and Ben Kingsley's Don Logan flying in to scream him back to London for one job — the terror is mostly conversational.

metas.name: Inside Man
metas.description: Captures a bank robbery as theatre with a purpose you have to wait for. Manhattan hostages dressed identically to the robbers, a detective and a fixer circling each other, and a heist whose real target isn't the money.

metas.name: Hell or High Water
metas.description: Captures two brothers robbing the bank that is taking their family's land. West Texas, foreclosed ranches and debt-relief billboards, and two ageing Rangers following them at the speed of talk — a western wearing a recession.

metas.name: Crash
metas.description: Captures desire re-wired through injury and machinery. After a serious collision on Toronto highways, a couple drift into a circle for whom crashes, scars and cars have become erotic — cold, deadpan and permanently controversial.

metas.name: Blue Is the Warmest Colour
metas.description: Captures first love at the resolution of skin, food and class difference. A schoolgirl in Lille and an older art student with blue hair — long scenes of eating, talking and teaching, and a breakup stretched across years of growing into different worlds.

metas.name: Secretary
metas.description: Captures kink as, for one specific person, a form of self-knowledge. A young woman fresh out of hospital for self-harm takes a typing job with a demanding lawyer, in a relationship the film treats as tender rather than a diagnosis.

metas.name: Lust, Caution
metas.description: Captures an espionage performance becoming the real feeling it was faking. In occupied Shanghai, a student actress is assigned to seduce a collaborationist official so he can be killed, over years of mahjong games and assignations.

metas.name: In the Realm of the Senses
metas.description: Captures obsession with the outside world switched off. 1930s Japan, a hotel maid and her employer in a room, in a spiral based on a real case — explicit as claustrophobia, not titillation.

metas.name: Touki Bouki
metas.description: Captures two young people dreaming of Paris so hard the film itself starts hallucinating. Senegal: a cowherd and a student steal and scheme toward a ship, on a motorbike with a skull mounted on it, in editing that jumps like a skipping song.

metas.name: Hyenas
metas.description: Captures a village discovering its price. A woman returns after decades, impossibly rich, offering her poor hometown a fortune for one act of 'justice' against the man who wronged her — while shops fill with goods bought on credit.

metas.name: Yeelen
metas.description: Captures a myth from inside its own cosmology. Mali, Bambara legend: a son fleeing his sorcerer father across desert and village, carrying stolen sacred objects, toward a confrontation filmed as light itself.

metas.name: Timbuktu
metas.description: Captures occupation resisted through music, football and dignity. Jihadists take a Malian town and ban singing and soccer; people comply in public, sing quietly at night, and play a match with an invisible ball.

metas.name: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
metas.description: Captures a vampire film rebuilt from Iranian, Western and skate-punk parts. A fictional Iranian ghost town, a chador-wearing vampire on a skateboard, a drug dealer and a cat, in long black-and-white silences between bursts of pop.

metas.name: Atlantics
metas.description: Captures young men who leave by sea returning in another form. Dakar construction workers, unpaid for months, take a boat toward Spain; the film stays with the women left behind, the sea at night, and a love story conducted through possession and fever.

metas.name: Pi
metas.description: Captures obsession with a pattern, filmed on grain. A mathematician in a tiny New York apartment with computers made of junk, a number that Wall Street and a Hasidic sect both want, and migraines rendered as drill sounds.

metas.name: Gummo
metas.description: Captures boredom and poverty in an American town as unconnected afternoons. Xenia, Ohio, after a tornado: kids sniffing, selling dead cats, taped monologues, no plot arriving to save anyone.

metas.name: George Washington
metas.description: Captures rural Southern childhood in the long light after something goes wrong. Kids in a decaying town carry an accident together, and a boy in a cape wants to be a hero — all voiceover and golden fields.
